page: Google Cloud Platform m4n-hypermem-16 is a dedicated virtual machine instance engineered with an emphasis on extreme memory density. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and provides 16 dedicated vCPUs paired with 248 GB of system memory, delivering a high allocation of 15.5 GB of RAM per core. The server configuration includes zero hardware accelerators and contains no local storage, requiring persistent operational data and operating systems to be hosted on external block storage volumes.

The 15.5 GB per vCPU allocation accommodates datasets that significantly exceed conventional cloud server memory-to-compute ratios. From a cost-efficiency perspective, this configuration allows organizations to fulfill large working-memory requirements without over-provisioning superfluous compute cores. However, the reliance on external network storage introduces dependencies on network storage bandwidth and latency, representing a clear operational tradeoff compared to instances with bundled local NVMe storage.

This instance configuration is targeted at workloads constrained primarily by resident memory footprints rather than raw computational density. Standard deployment profiles include distributed in-memory data grids, large Redis or Memcached instances, enterprise relational databases managing extensive active working sets, and memory-bound extract, transform, load pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform m4n-hypermem-16 is a specialized, memory-dense virtual machine architecture featuring 16 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 248 GB of system RAM, yielding a high ratio of 15.5 GB of memory per core. As an accelerator-free instance without bundled local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, the server is engineered for workloads where raw memory capacity and dedicated compute stability are paramount. Storage requirements must be satisfied through attached remote volumes, positioning disk throughput on network storage interfaces. By offering extreme memory density against a moderate core count, the instance prevents compute over-allocation for memory-heavy footprints. The m4n-hypermem-16 is suited for large in-memory caches, distributed memory stores, enterprise database instances, and real-time data processing pipelines that require substantial resident datasets without necessitating extreme multi-core parallelism.
